final_candidates.decision_summary: ESM-1v strongly favors this conservative Glu-to-Asp change and ProteinMPNN accepts it well on the 3D11 backbone; MSA is neutral without a contraindication. Its surface location may modestly tune receptor contacts while preserving fold.

High sequence plausibility and acceptable structural compatibility support an isosteric longer-acidic-side-chain mutation. It is retained as a conservative candidate for altered electrostatic interactions at the head surface.

Substantial ESM-1v plausibility and moderate ProteinMPNN compatibility make this hydrophobic packing substitution a reasonable choice; the hydrophobic core/local interface impact is limited by the conservative Val-to-Ile size increase.

stop_reason.detail: No phenotype predictor is available and the remaining tools are static or safety-side; additional evidence would not materially revise the already stable Top-3 ranking.

history.rationale: Larger hydrophobic side chain in the ephrin-binding pocket may increase buried surface area and van der Waals contacts, improving receptor engagement.
Sequence plausibility is moderate, but structural compatibility is poor and no evolutionary support exists. Confidence is lowered accordingly.
Retain with current confidence; PLM decent but structure and evolution weaker, functional annotation neutral.
Adds hydrophobic bulk to the receptor-contact patch without altering backbone positioning, potentially improving ephrin binding affinity.
Very high sequence plausibility and a conservative hydrophobic substitution boost confidence despite lack of evolutionary observation. Promoted above N459A.
Retain based on moderate PLM and structure support; functional annotation does not change ranking.
Introduces an aromatic group near the critical Tyr511 region, potentially enhancing pi-stacking or hydrophobic complementarity with ephrin.
High sequence plausibility and non-zero evolutionary frequency suggest moderate promise. Structural compatibility is below average but not prohibitive.
Retain as fifth option; PLM and structure scores moderate, functional annotation provides no additional signal.
Fills a plausible unoccupied hydrophobic cavity at the C-terminal receptor-binding loop, potentially stabilizing the bound conformation.
Good structural compatibility and moderate sequence plausibility support a slight retention. Lack of evolutionary support prevents a higher confidence.
Keep in pool; structure score moderate, but low PLM and evolutionary tolerance, functional annotation does not clarify.
Preserves positive charge while providing a larger guanidinium group, which may strengthen electrostatic interactions with ephrin.
Good structural compatibility and moderate sequence plausibility support a moderate confidence increase, but evolutionary evidence is minimal. Retained in the active pool.
Retain; structure compatibility good, but lower PLM and evolutionary support, functional annotation neutral.
Removes a potentially steric N-linked glycan that could shield receptor-binding surfaces, likely increasing effective binding accessibility.
All three tools score poorly for this substitution, so it is demoted substantially. No evidence currently supports this candidate.
Retain as low-priority; functional annotation indicates head region but no effect direction, keep in pool in case no better candidates.
Deletion of another glycan site on the head domain may reduce steric interference and improve attachment to ephrin receptors.
Low sequence plausibility and zero evolutionary support outweigh decent structural compatibility. Confidence is reduced to reflect the weak overall profile.
Retain with lowest confidence; structure moderate, but PLM low, functional annotation neutral.
Removing this glycosylation site in a flexible loop may reduce glycan bulk and enhance conformational sampling of the receptor-binding surface.
Structural compatibility is the highest among the tested candidates and there is some evolutionary support. This mutation is promoted.
Structure compatibility is high and some evolutionary tolerance observed; functional annotation neutral, keep in top 4.
Shortening the carboxylate side chain could tighten interfacial hydrogen bonding or electrostatic geometry without losing charge.
Top sequence plausibility and strong structural compatibility make this the leading candidate. Evolutionary absence is discounted due to shallow alignment coverage.
Functional annotation confirms position 509 is in the head region and disulfide-bond-containing domain, but provides no effect direction; retain top rank based on strong PLM and structure scores.
Extending the carboxylate chain may permit more favorable electrostatic/hydrogen-bonding interactions at the receptor interface.
High sequence plausibility and moderate structural compatibility support a strong ranking. No evolutionary support but the evolutionary evidence is weak overall.
Functional annotation is neutral, but PLM and structure scores remain favorable; keep second rank.
